title: Normative data for modified Ferriman-Gallwey score and the prevalence of hirsutism in young South Indians
recruitment_notes: Multi-stage sampling: 6 apartment societies randomly chosen, alternate flats visited, one eligible woman per flat chosen at random; examined at home. Women of western, eastern or northern Indian origin excluded. STROBE flowchart in Fig 1.
assessor_notes: Two investigators (described as trained medical students in the abstract) trained for 1 month by an endocrinologist; validated on 100 women; inter-observer kappa 0.927-0.951.
mfg_method_notes: Modified FG score; 9 androgen-sensitive sites per Introduction (max 36).
cutoff_notes: Derived as the 97.5th centile in women without a PCOS phenotype (n about 399-401) = 5; same value in non-obese, overweight and normal-BMI subgroups; obese non-PCOS subgroup = 6; whole-sample 97.5th centile = 7. Methods say upper limit of the '97.5% CI' while Results say '97.5th centile' (inconsistent wording). No ROC or cluster analysis.
quality_notes: Strengths: community sample, random selection, trained assessors with reported agreement. Limits: young sample (mean 22); not pan-India (excludes western, eastern and northern origin); cutoff comes from a subgroup rather than the whole sample. Median 1 (IQR 0-3). All 8 women at >=8 had another PCOS-related feature. Table 1 labels the non-PCOS group n=401 but Results text uses 399.
data_source: PMC full-text PDF (PMC11451954); AI-assisted extraction, needs human check against the PDF
notes: Introduction also contains the contested claim that a South Asian cutoff of >=4 is lower than in Caucasians (cited to a Thai study); see claims.csv C01. Source of the Kashmir lead (zargar_kashmir_unverified).

title: Modified Ferriman-Gallwey score and hirsutism among normal healthy female population
recruitment_notes: Married women aged 20-40 attending the outpatient department, called 'normal healthy' on the basis of a normal conception history (used as a proxy for normal hormones). Apr-Oct 2022. Sampling method (consecutive, random) not stated. Exclusions: fertility problems, menstrual irregularity, endocrine or chronic disease, hirsutism treatment or drugs causing hirsutism.
assessor_notes: Who scored and how they were trained are not reported; text says visual assessment following Ferriman and Gallwey.
mfg_method_notes: Methods list 10 regions; Introduction and Table II use 9. Methods say the total was 'averaged' but the regional means in Table II sum to about 8.9, so the total looks like a sum.
cutoff_notes: >=8 in Methods and Table III; abstract Results wording is 'more than 8'. Authors argue a local cutoff above 8 may be needed but do not derive one.
quality_notes: Check against the PDF before relying on these figures: (1) 255/448 (56.9%) appears both as hirsutism prevalence and as cream-depilatory use in Table I; (2) some Table II regional means do not match the printed score counts (e.g. upper lip, lower abdomen) per the extraction tool; (3) no assessor or sampling detail; (4) severity bands not defined (mild 52.0%, moderate 4.5%, severe 0.4% of the whole sample). Hospital OPD, married women only, 'healthy' defined by fertility history.
data_source: PMC full text (PMC10862439); AI-assisted extraction, needs human check against the PDF
notes: Median mFG not reported. Mean 8.89 is far above Josyula's community mean of 1.81, which is the kind of gap the database is meant to expose.

title: Prevalence and patterns of hirsutism among Sri Lankan females
journal: Sri Lanka J Diabetes Endocrinol Metab 2015;5:51-5
recruitment_notes: 85 female medical students entering the university in 2000; cross-sectional, data collected in 2000. 3 (3.5%) had menstrual irregularity; none had used steroids or psoralens.
assessor_notes: Each subject was interviewed by a medical officer (interviewer-administered questionnaire); the abstract does not say who scored the mFG.
cutoff_notes: Abstract does not say which mFG threshold produced the 56.5% prevalence (95% CI 45.96-67.04). Read the full PDF. Implied count is about 48/85.
quality_notes: Abstract only so far. Mode 5.0, IQR 5-11. Convenience sample of medical students; data 15 years old at publication.
data_source: Journal abstract page (full-text PDF not yet read)
notes: Probable overlap with Somasundaram, Malavige and Kamaladasa 2005, Sri Lanka J Dermatol 9(1):16-17 (screening record SL04): same university entrants. Resolve before counting them as separate evidence.
